h1: The 6 Best Printers for Homeschooling of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six printers for homeschool families, from refillable ink tanks to a mono laser, sorted by running cost and scanning.
summary: The Epson EcoTank ET-2400 is our top pick for families that print worksheets in color every week. The Brother DCP-L2640DW wins for black-and-white-heavy curricula, and the Canon PIXMA TR4720 is the best choice if you scan graded work in stacks. The HP DeskJet 4355 is the cheapest way to start while you learn your real print volume.
intro: Most homeschool parents pick a printer by its sticker price, then spend the next year paying for ink. A curriculum that spits out 20 to 40 pages a day turns a cheap cartridge printer into the most expensive device in the house. The decision that matters is how the printer stores and charges for ink, not how many apps it supports.

We ranked six printers that fit a kitchen table or a school shelf, judging them on paper from the spec sheets and owner reports. Running cost, duplex printing, scanning with a document feeder, and wireless setup counted most. Prices are shown as buckets because they move constantly.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-2400 Wireless Cartridge-Free Supertank Printer
products.verdict: The printer that stops ink from being your biggest homeschool expense.
products.description:
The ET-2400 swaps cartridges for refillable tanks filled from bottles, and bottled ink is included at setup. It prints, scans, and copies in color over Wi-Fi, and it costs $100-200.

First place goes to it because the ink system is the one feature that changes the math for a family printing every day. The pick below it, the Brother laser, is cheaper per page for text, but the ET-2400 is the only one here that handles color diagrams, maps, and art pages without a penalty.

Buy it if you have one to three kids and a steady stream of worksheets. The caveat is that it has no automatic document feeder in its listed specs, so scanning a stack of finished pages means feeding the glass one sheet at a time.
products.idealFor: Families printing color and black-and-white pages every week.
products.skipIf: You print a handful of pages a month.

products.name: Brother DCP-L2640DW Wireless Compact Monochrome Laser
products.verdict: A text-first workhorse that never dries out between school terms.
products.description:
This is a monochrome laser with automatic two-sided printing, plus built-in copy and scan, over wireless and mobile connections. The footprint is small enough for a homeschool desk. Budget $200-500.

Laser toner does not clog the way inkjet nozzles do during a summer break, which is the real reason it ranks second. It loses first place to the ET-2400 only because it cannot print color, so science diagrams and graded art come out gray.

Choose it for math, grammar, and reading programs that live in black and white. If your curriculum leans on color charts, a second device or a different pick is the honest answer.
products.idealFor: Text-heavy curricula with daily black-and-white worksheets.
products.skipIf: Your lessons rely on color printouts.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: The affordable pick for parents who archive every graded page.
products.description:
The TR4720 is a color inkjet all-in-one with an auto document feeder, mobile printing, wireless connectivity, and a legacy fax function. Budget $50-100.

The feeder is what lifts it above the DeskJet 4355 below it: scanning a week of finished worksheets into a portfolio takes one load instead of thirty glass lifts. It ranks under the Brother and Epson because its ink comes in cartridges, so heavy printing costs more over time.

Pick it if record keeping for your state matters as much as printing. Skip it if you expect to print more than a few dozen pages a week.
products.idealFor: Parents who scan stacks of graded worksheets.
products.skipIf: You print more than a few dozen pages weekly.

products.name: Epson Workforce WF-2930 Wireless All-in-One Printer
products.verdict: Duplex and a feeder on one budget inkjet, with cartridge ink as the price.
products.description:
The WF-2930 prints, scans, copies, and faxes in color, with an automatic document feeder, automatic two-sided printing, and a 1.4-inch color display. It costs $50-100.

It is the only cartridge model here that pairs a feeder with true automatic duplex, so it edges the TR4720 for families that print front and back to save paper. It ranks fourth because cartridges still make a heavy printing year pricey next to an ink-tank model.

Good for moderate daily printing plus multi-page scans. The small display means setup and troubleshooting happen mostly from a phone or computer.
products.idealFor: Moderate printing with paper-saving duplex and multi-page scans.
products.skipIf: You print heavy color every day.

products.award: Best Ink Tank on a Tight Budget
products.name: HP Smart Tank 5101 Wireless All-in-One Refillable Printer
products.verdict: Tank-style savings with a small footprint, minus a document feeder.
products.description:
The Smart Tank 5101 uses refillable ink tanks, ships with two years of ink in the listing, and prints, scans, and copies over 2.4GHz wireless. Budget $100-200.

It competes directly with the Epson ET-2400 and lands a notch lower because the listing stresses 2.4GHz-only Wi-Fi, which can complicate setup on routers that merge bands. The tradeoff is a compact body that fits tighter school corners.

A fit for budget-minded families who still want tank economics. Check your router before buying, and expect to scan one sheet at a time.
products.idealFor: Tank savings for a family on a tighter budget.
products.skipIf: Your router only offers a combined 5GHz network.

products.name: HP DeskJet 4355 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A low-risk way to learn your real print volume first.
products.description:
HP's DeskJet 4355 handles color printing, scanning and copying over Wi-Fi in a small body, and the listing adds a three-month Instant Ink trial. Expect to pay $50-100.

Last place follows because its strengths are price and size, not capability: no feeder or duplex is listed, and cartridge ink is the costliest route over a school year. Its value is as a trial run before committing to a tank or laser.

Buy it for a first year of homeschooling or a light curriculum. Plan to upgrade once your monthly page count settles.
products.idealFor: New homeschoolers testing their real print volume.

whatMatters.detail: Cartridge printers sell hardware cheaply and make money on refills, while tank printers use bottled ink that costs far less per page. For a family printing daily, that gap outweighs the upfront price. Check the listing for words like refillable, tank, or EcoTank rather than assuming a printer is economical.

A monochrome laser is excellent for text but prints every diagram in gray. Decide whether your curriculum truly needs color science, maps, and art pages. Skim your curriculum's sample pages before deciding.

A feeder pulls a stack of sheets through the scanner so you do not lift the lid for each page. It matters when you scan graded work for records. Look for the words automatic document feeder in the specs, since many models skip it.
Automatic two-sided printing halves paper use and shortens thick packets. Manual duplex means flipping pages yourself. Look for automatic 2-sided in the listing.

Some tank printers connect only on the 2.4GHz band, which trips up routers that combine bands under one name. Check your router settings before purchase. The listing usually states the band in the feature bullets.

howToChoose.intro: How much you print each week usually decides which technology pays off.

cards.label: Ink tank
cards.text: Bottled ink refills the tanks and costs much less per page. The Epson EcoTank ET-2400 and HP Smart Tank 5101 use it.

cards.label: Cartridge
cards.text: Cheaper to buy, pricier to run. The Canon PIXMA TR4720, Epson Workforce WF-2930, and HP DeskJet 4355 use cartridges.

howToChoose.note: Default to a tank if you print weekly; pick a cartridge model only for light or trial use.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Mobile printing support and a Wi-Fi band your router can serve.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Canon PIXMA TR4720 lists mobile printing, and the Epson EcoTank ET-2400 and Brother DCP-L2640DW both print wirelessly.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You print daily or in color; the Epson EcoTank ET-2400 or Brother DCP-L2640DW repays the difference in ink savings.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You are in a first year; the HP DeskJet 4355 or Canon PIXMA TR4720 is enough.

faq.q: Is a laser or inkjet better for homeschooling?
faq.a: A laser such as the Brother DCP-L2640DW is better for black-and-white text because toner stays usable between school terms. An inkjet or ink tank is better when you need color.

faq.q: Do I need a document feeder?
faq.a: Only if you scan stacks of graded work. The Canon PIXMA TR4720 and Epson Workforce WF-2930 list feeders.

faq.q: Is an ink tank printer worth it over a cheap inkjet?
faq.a: If you print weekly, yes. The Epson EcoTank ET-2400 costs more upfront but bottled ink is far cheaper than cartridges.

faq.q: Why won't my HP Smart Tank 5101 connect?
faq.a: It works on 2.4GHz Wi-Fi only. Turn on the 2.4GHz band on your router or separate the band names during setup.

faq.q: How do I keep inkjet nozzles from clogging?
faq.a: Print a color page every week or two. Long idle spells are where inkjets suffer and lasers do not.

faq.q: Can I use these with an iPad?
faq.a: Most list wireless and mobile printing. The Canon PIXMA TR4720 specifically mentions mobile printing support.

finalTake: For most homeschool families, the Epson EcoTank ET-2400 is the one that removes the ongoing ink worry. Text-only households should take the Brother DCP-L2640DW, and record keepers should take the Canon PIXMA TR4720. The HP DeskJet 4355 is a fine first-year gamble.
